trajectory_messages.content:
I'm running into a bug with field array validation.

*   When a resolver returns both a root-level error on a field array (an object with type and message properties) and nested per-item errors (indexed entries with field-level errors) for the same array field simultaneously, the form state must store and expose both types of errors at the same time — root error accessible via errors.fieldName.type and errors.fieldName.message, and item errors accessible via errors.fieldName[index].fieldProperty.

*   After an item is removed from a field array and validation is re-triggered, root-level array errors (those with type and message on the array itself) must remain visible in the form error state.

*   After an item is removed from a field array and validation is re-triggered, nested per-item field errors must be re-indexed to reflect the updated item positions — an item that shifts from index N to index M due to a removal must have its errors appear at the new index M.

*   When both root-level and item-level errors coexist for the same field array, performing a remove operation followed by re-validation must not cause existing item-level errors to be silently dropped — all errors that the resolver returns must be reflected in the form error state.


**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

All green. Here's what I changed and why.

## The bug

In `src/useFieldArray.ts`, after a field-array mutation (like `remove`) triggers resolver re-validation, the code decided whether to write the fresh resolver errors into form state using this check:

```js
existingError
  ? (!error && existingError.type) ||
    (error &&
      (existingError.type !== error.type ||
        existingError.message !== error.message))
  : error && error.type
```

This only compares the **root** error's `type`/`message`. When a field array has *both* a root error (`errors.test.type`/`.message`) and per-item errors (`errors.test[index].field`), a `remove` re-indexes the item errors but leaves the root `type`/`message` identical. The condition evaluated to `false`, so `set(...)` never ran — the stale, wrongly-indexed item errors were left in place (and in some flows dropped entirely).

## The fix

Compare the full existing error against the freshly-resolved error with `deepEqual`, so *any* difference — including changed or re-indexed item-level errors — triggers the update:

```js
existingError
  ? !deepEqual(existingError, error)
  : error && error.type
```

When they differ, the branch still does `set(control._formState.errors, name, error)`, which writes the resolver's complete error object (root `type`/`message` **and** all indexed item errors) verbatim. This satisfies all four requirements:

- Root and item errors coexist and are both stored/exposed (they're set from the resolver's combined object).
- Root errors survive a remove (they're re-set as long as the resolver still returns them, never spuriously unset).
- Item errors get re-indexed to their new positions on remove.
- No item errors are silently dropped, since `deepEqual` now catches item-only changes that the old `type`/`message`-only check missed.

`deepEqual` ignores `ref` keys, so this doesn't introduce spurious re-renders, and once state matches the resolver output the comparison stabilizes (no update loop).

I only touched source (`src/useFieldArray.ts` — added the `deepEqual` import and rewrote the condition); the `tests/` directory was left untouched. Typecheck passes and all 742 relevant tests pass.
